name: JRC LUCAS cover photos 2006-2018
use: 874,646 geo-tagged close-up land-cover photos with land-cover and plant species labels. Pre-training / linear-probe corpus for vegetation and bare-soil labels. EU only, so a domain-shift source, never a test set.
licence: JRC open data (CC-BY-4.0 paper, ESSD doi:10.5194/essd-14-4463-2022)

name: JRC Harmonised LUCAS in-situ database
use: The survey table behind the photos: 1,351,293 observations at 651,780 locations. Joins photo -> land-cover label -> coordinates.

name: LUCAS landscape photos, ML-ready (Source Cooperative)
use: Agri-environmental semantic segmentation of LUCAS landscape photos. Closest public analogue to a DRISHTI landscape geotag: observer-view photographs of agricultural land with per-pixel labels.
licence: Check per-repository terms on Source Cooperative

name: Mapillary street-level imagery API v4
use: REJECTED for GT-1 after measurement. Coverage in the 7 candidate Marathwada districts is 0-5% of 2.2 km cells and follows national highways only; sampled frames are windscreen dashcam views of divided carriageway, crash barriers and sky. Watershed structures are off-highway by definition, so this source cannot supply the GT-1 label set. Retained only as a marginal source for nala culverts where a highway crosses a drainage line. See the measured table below.
licence: CC-BY-SA 4.0 (verified on Mapillary's licence page). ShareAlike means derived annotation sets must be shared alike - fine for us, we publish GT-1 anyway.

name: Wikimedia Commons geosearch API
use: Mineable, not a dataset: geotagged CC-licensed photographs. Useful for check dams, percolation tanks and stepwells where Mapillary has no road access. Every file's licence must be read individually.
detail: control (Paris 10 km) 500 files; demo AOI (19.15N 77.30E, 10 km) 41 files — genuinely sparse, not a query error. On-topic categories total ~283 files: Check dams in India=14; Dams in Maharashtra=108; Ponds in India=42; Water tanks in India=46; Stepwells in India=15; Irrigation in India=58. Radius is capped at 10000 m; larger values return empty, not more data.

name: Places365 scene classification
use: WOULD be useful for zero-shot prompt calibration (categories include creek, farm, cultivated field, fishpond). Two blockers: access is now form-gated, and the licence is non-commercial research only - which constraint C-7 already forbids as a production dependency.
licence: Non-commercial research/education only -> cannot be a production dependency for a government system (same rule that excludes GEE, C-7)
detail: download page no longer offers direct archives: access to the legacy dataset now requires signing a Google Form while v2 is in progress

name: AgriFieldNet India (Radiant Earth / IDinsight)
use: Sentinel-2 crop-type labels for fields in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Odisha and Bihar. Not watershed structures, but the only India-specific labelled EO reference set found - useful to sanity-check our seasonal NDVI compositing against independent Indian crop labels.

name: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API
use: Candidate GT-2 seed. VERDICT: unusable for check dams (see the measured counts in the notes below), partially usable for ponds and water bodies. Production route is a Geofabrik India extract, not the live API.

name: Geofabrik India OSM extract
use: The reliable way to use OSM at scale: download the India .osm.pbf once and query locally with osmium, instead of hammering Overpass.

name: Bhuvan WMS — IWMP district drainage + PMKSY waterbodies
use: The W3 fix's reference layer, and it is authoritative NRSC data: per-district drainage networks to calibrate the flow-accumulation stream-initiation threshold against, plus PMKSY waterbody polygons as an independent GT-2 water reference. WMS raster only - no WFS - so calibration compares rasterised masks, not vector geometries.
licence: NRSC terms; view/overlay use. Attribution required.
detail: 5306 layers total; 24 Maharashtra district drainage layers (e.g. iwmp:MH_AKOLA_drn, iwmp:MH_AMRAVATI_drn, iwmp:MH_AURANGABAD_drn); 6 waterbody layers (incl. pmksy:pmksy_waterbodes_lulc50k1112). WFS advertises 0 feature types, so vector download is UNAVAILABLE - use WMS GetMap and compare as raster masks.

name: JRC Global Surface Water
use: Already in the design (docs §12): 30 m multi-decadal water occurrence. Doubles as an independent GT-2 reference for the waterbody_renovation type, which is why that type carries an L4 ceiling.
